props.title: Thriller: A Cruel Picture

sections.content: **Thriller: A Cruel Picture** (1973), also known as "They Call Her One Eye," stands as one of the most controversial Swedish exploitation films ever made. Director Bo Arne Vibenius crafted this ultra-violent revenge tale that directly influenced Quentin Tarantino's **Kill Bill Vol. 1** (2003), particularly the Elle Driver character. The film follows Christina, a mute woman who suffers horrific abuse before methodically training herself in combat to exact revenge. Like **I Spit on Your Grave** (1978) and **Ms .45** (1981), it belongs to the rape-revenge subgenre that emerged in the 1970s, though its extreme content and real ammunition used in filming make it particularly notorious.

sections.content: The film's technical elements deserve examination despite its controversial content. Vibenius employed unique slow-motion photography shooting at 500 frames per second, creating hyper-detailed violence that would influence later action films. Christina Lindberg's portrayal became iconic in exploitation cinema, though she later expressed regret about some scenes. The film shares DNA with **The Last House on the Left** (1972) and **Death Wish** (1974) in examining vigilante justice, though through a distinctly European arthouse-meets-grindhouse lens. SUBHEAD: Impact on Modern Cinema

The film's influence extends beyond just Tarantino. Modern revenge thrillers like **The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo** (2009) and **Revenge** (2017) echo its themes of female vengeance while treating sexual violence with more gravity. **Drive** (2011) borrowed its aesthetic of methodical violence punctuated by extreme moments. Even mainstream films like **John Wick** (2014) draw from its portrayal of a wronged protagonist meticulously training for revenge.
